title: Forced Out Twice: The Story of Calgary's Chinatown
topic_used: Calgary's Chinatown in three locations: first just east of the train station (today's Calgary Municipal Building); 1892 smallpox outbreak fuelled violence, a mob of over 300 smashed Chinese laundries' doors and windows, NWMP protected Chinatown for three weeks; from 1901 a second Chinatown across the tracks on 10 Ave SW (anti-Chinese sentiment and development pressure, CBC); 1910 Canadian Northern Railway route announced, property values soared, landlords evicted Chinese tenants and sold; Chinese merchants bought land at Centre St & 2 Ave, anti-Chinese protesters demanded it be elsewhere, they won a permit and built the Canton Block (1910-11, 200-216 Centre St SE, still standing); 1966 parkway would have eliminated half of Chinatown, defeated by Sien Lok; Cultural Centre 1992, modelled on the Temple of Heaven; there since 1910.
changed_from_calendar: Kept the subject; reframed 'three moves' to three locations / two forced moves (City of Calgary). No founding year used (sources say 1883/1885/1888/c.1890).
central_figure: Chinatown 'has been in three different locations in Calgary' (City of Calgary, Tomorrow's Chinatown); the Canton Block (1910-11) still stands (Heritage Calgary)

title: Almost Fort Brisebois: Why It's Called Calgary
topic_used: How Calgary got its name: the 1875 NWMP fort at the Bow-Elbow confluence was first 'The Elbow', then 'Fort Brisebois' (named by Inspector Brisebois after himself, by Jan 1876); Assistant Commissioner Irvine cancelled the order and wrote to Ottawa on Feb 29, 1876 that Colonel Macleod supported 'Calgary' ('which I believe in Scotch means clear running water'); Macleod took it from a favourite place on the Isle of Mull (Calgary Bay); Mull guides translate the Gaelic as 'beach of the meadow' / 'the meadow beside the bay'; approved by Ottawa, confirmed April 1876; Brisebois quit in August; Brisebois Drive NW; 150 years in 2026
central_figure: Irvine's letter to Ottawa, Feb. 29, 1876: 'Colonel Macleod has supported the name of Calgary which I believe in Scotch means clear running water' (City of Calgary Archives, via City of Calgary Newsroom)
